questions.title: Point on the perpendicular bisector
questions.text: The point which lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points A(−3, −4) and B(3, 4) is:
steps: ① Perpendicular bisector cuts AB at its mid-point, at 90°
④ Every point on it is equidistant from A and B
questions.remember:
Mid-point = ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2)
Every point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from A and B.
questions.trap: Using the distance formula on every option. The mid-point is on the bisector, so start there.
questions.tryit: Find the mid-point of (5, −4) and (6, 4). On which axis does it lie?

questions.title: Radius from a diameter's end points
questions.text: The end points of a diameter of a circle are (2, 4) and (−3, −1). The length of its radius is:
questions.trap: Stopping at the diameter (5√2) and picking option (b). The question asks for the RADIUS.

questions.title: Length of median PM
questions.text: PM is a median of △PQR with vertices P(5, −6), Q(6, 4) and R(0, 0). The length of PM is:
steps: ① Median: vertex to the MID-POINT of the opposite side
questions.remember: A median joins a vertex to the mid-point of the OPPOSITE side.
questions.trap: Taking the mid-point of PQ or PR. It must be the side opposite P: QR.
questions.tryit: Find the length of the median from R in the same triangle.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: fourth vertex of a parallelogram
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If three vertices of a parallelogram taken in order are (−1, −6), (2, −5) and (7, 2), then its fourth vertex is (4, 1).
Reason (R): Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① R: diagonals of a ∥gm bisect each other  ✓ true
③ Mid-point of BD = ((2 + x)/2, (−5 + y)/2)
④ Same mid-point ⟹ x = 4,  y = 1 ⟹ D(4, 1)  ✓ A true
⑤ D was found USING R
questions.remember: Parallelogram ABCD: mid-point of AC = mid-point of BD.
questions.trap: Pairing the wrong vertices. 'Taken in order' means A–C and B–D are the diagonals.
questions.tryit: (1, 2), (4, y), (x, 6), (3, 5) are the vertices of a parallelogram in order. Find x and y.

questions.title: Do P, Q, R form a triangle?
questions.text: Do the points P(1, 0), Q(−5, 0) and R(−2, 5) form a triangle? If so, name the type of triangle formed.
steps: ④ QR + PR > PQ ⟹ not on one line ⟹ triangle
questions.remember: Two sides equal → isosceles. Check a² + b² = c² for right-angled.
questions.trap: Naming the type without showing all three distances. Each one carries marks.
questions.tryans: No: the distances don't add up

questions.title: Centre (x − 7, 2x), radius 5√2
questions.text: The coordinates of the centre of a circle are (x − 7, 2x). Find the value(s) of 'x', if the circle passes through the point (−9, 11) and has radius 5√2 units.
steps: ① Centre C(x − 7, 2x), point P(−9, 11), CP = radius = 5√2
⑤ Check: centres (−4, 6) and (−2, 10), both 5√2 away ✓
questions.remember: Square both sides first, so there are no roots to handle.
questions.trap: Keeping only one value of x. Both centres are exactly 5√2 away, so both are correct.
questions.tryit: Find y if the distance between (2, −3) and (10, y) is 10.

questions.title: Ratio in which the x-axis divides AB
questions.text: In what ratio does the x-axis divide the line segment joining the points (−4, −6) and (−1, 7)? Also, find the coordinates of the point of division.
steps: ① On the x-axis ⟹ y = 0 · point P(x, 0), ratio k : 1
questions.remember:
On the x-axis, y = 0. On the y-axis, x = 0.
Section formula: (m x₂ + n x₁)/(m + n)
questions.trap: Swapping x₁ and x₂ in the section formula. m goes with the SECOND point.
questions.tryit: In what ratio does (−1, 6) divide the join of (−3, 10) and (6, −8)?

questions.title: Ratio in which the y-axis divides AB
questions.text: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the line segment joining the points (5, −6) and (−1, −4). Also find the point of intersection.
steps: ① On the y-axis ⟹ x = 0 · point P(0, y), ratio k : 1
questions.remember: x-axis ⟹ use the y-coordinates. y-axis ⟹ use the x-coordinates.
questions.trap: Setting y = 0 for the y-axis. On the y-axis it's x that is zero.
questions.tryit: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the join of (−3, 4) and (6, −2).
